answer: Time-cost gating makes sybil attacks expensive without any money changing hands: a new identity earns full rights only after a long, enforced waiting period of continuous activity, so an attacker must pay in weeks, not coins. A vine of linked activity records proves the waiting was real and cannot be fast-forwarded. Each pearl of reputation is earned slowly, and juniper-style rotation of verification challenges prevents pre-computed identities from skipping the queue. Mass-producing sock puppets fails because time, unlike tokens, cannot be bought in bulk.
